Landslide Segmentation on EO Imagery¶

U-Net vs FCN/DeepLab vs Transformer (Landslide4Sense)¶

Objective¶

This notebook presents a structured comparison of semantic segmentation architectures for landslide detection using multispectral Earth Observation (EO) imagery.

We evaluate:

  • U-Net (custom baseline)
  • FCN-ResNet50
  • DeepLabV3-ResNet50
  • U-Net (TorchGeo)
  • SegFormer-B0 (transformer-based)
  • Swin Transformer (UPerNet)

Goal: understand the trade-offs between classical CNN-based segmentation, encoder–decoder architectures, and transformer-based models under multispectral input, small-data conditions and controlled setup.

Workflow¶

  1. Data loading
  2. Image Preprocessing
  3. Model training (6 architectures)
  4. Evaluation and comparison (OA, F1, mean F1)
  5. Visualization (predictions vs. ground truth masks)

Dataset¶

We use a subset of the Landslide4Sense dataset:

  • 14-channel input (spectral + topographic)
    • 12 multispectral bands from Sentinel-2 (B1–B12)
    • 1 slope band derived from ALOS PALSAR (B13)
    • 1 elevation band (DEM) from ALOS PALSAR (B14)
  • Pixel-wise annotations (landslide vs. non-landslide)
  • Image–mask pairs (~10 m resolution, 128 × 128 patches)

The dataset is split into training and test sets.
(ref: https://github.com/iarai/Landslide4Sense-2022)

# Visualization
import h5py

def index2bgr_z(c_map):

    # mapping W x H x 1 class index to W x H x 3 BGR image
    im_col, im_row = np.shape(c_map)
    c_map_r = np.ones((im_col, im_row), 'uint8')*255
    c_map_g = np.ones((im_col, im_row), 'uint8')*255
    c_map_b = np.ones((im_col, im_row), 'uint8')*255
    c_map_r[c_map == 1] = 255
    c_map_g[c_map == 1] = 30
    c_map_b[c_map == 1] = 30

    c_map_rgb = np.zeros((im_col, im_row, 3), 'uint8')
    c_map_rgb[:, :, 0] = c_map_r
    c_map_rgb[:, :, 1] = c_map_g
    c_map_rgb[:, :, 2] = c_map_b
    
    return c_map_rgb

In [4]:
# Data loader
from tqdm import tqdm

class LandslideDataSet(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, data_dir, list_path, max_iters=None,set='labeled'):
        self.list_path = list_path
        self.mean = [-0.4914, -0.3074, -0.1277, -0.0625, 0.0439, 0.0803, 0.0644, 0.0802, 0.3000, 0.4082, 0.0823, 0.0516, 0.3338, 0.7819]
        self.std = [0.9325, 0.8775, 0.8860, 0.8869, 0.8857, 0.8418, 0.8354, 0.8491, 0.9061, 1.6072, 0.8848, 0.9232, 0.9018, 1.2913]
        self.set = set
        self.img_ids = [i_id.strip() for i_id in open(list_path)]
        
        if not max_iters==None:
            n_repeat = int(np.ceil(max_iters / len(self.img_ids)))
            self.img_ids = self.img_ids * n_repeat + self.img_ids[:max_iters-n_repeat*len(self.img_ids)]

        self.files = []

        if set=='labeled':
            for name in self.img_ids:
                img_file = data_dir + name
                label_file = data_dir + name.replace('img','mask').replace('image','mask')
                self.files.append({
                    'img': img_file,
                    'label': label_file,
                    'name': name
                })
        elif set=='unlabeled':
            for name in self.img_ids:
                img_file = data_dir + name
                self.files.append({
                    'img': img_file,
                    'name': name
                })
            
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.files)


    def __getitem__(self, index):
        datafiles = self.files[index]
        
        if self.set=='labeled':
            with h5py.File(datafiles['img'], 'r') as hf:
                image = hf['img'][:]
            with h5py.File(datafiles['label'], 'r') as hf:
                label = hf['mask'][:]
            name = datafiles['name']
                
            image = np.asarray(image, np.float32)
            label = np.asarray(label, np.float32)
            
            image = image.transpose((-1, 0, 1))
            size = image.shape

            for i in range(len(self.mean)):
                image[i,:,:] -= self.mean[i]
                image[i,:,:] /= self.std[i]

            return image.copy(), label.copy(), np.array(size), name

        else:
            with h5py.File(datafiles['img'], 'r') as hf:
                image = hf['img'][:]
            name = datafiles['name']
                
            image = np.asarray(image, np.float32)
            image = image.transpose((-1, 0, 1))
            size = image.shape

            for i in range(len(self.mean)):
                image[i,:,:] -= self.mean[i]
                image[i,:,:] /= self.std[i]

            return image.copy(), np.array(size), name

Model training (6 architectures)¶

U-Net (custom baseline), FCN-ResNet50, DeepLabV3-ResNet50, U-Net (TorchGeo), SegFormer-B0 (transformer-based), and Swin Transformer (UPerNet) are trained under a unified pipeline.

In [8]:
# U-Net 
class DoubleConv(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, mid_channels=None):
        super().__init__()
        if not mid_channels:
            mid_channels = out_channels
        self.double_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_channels, mid_channels, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(mid_channels),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
            nn.Conv2d(mid_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(out_channels),
            nn.ReLU(inplace=True)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.double_conv(x)

class Down(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels):
        super().__init__()
        self.maxpool_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.MaxPool2d(2),
            DoubleConv(in_channels, out_channels)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.maxpool_conv(x)

class Up(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, bilinear=True):
        super().__init__()

        if bilinear:
            self.up = nn.Upsample(scale_factor=2, mode='bilinear', align_corners=True)
            self.conv = DoubleConv(in_channels, out_channels, in_channels // 2)
        else:
            self.up = nn.ConvTranspose2d(in_channels, in_channels // 2, kernel_size=2, stride=2)
            self.conv = DoubleConv(in_channels, out_channels)

    def forward(self, x1, x2):
        x1 = self.up(x1)
        diffY = x2.size()[2] - x1.size()[2]
        diffX = x2.size()[3] - x1.size()[3]

        x1 = F.pad(x1, [diffX // 2, diffX - diffX // 2,
                        diffY // 2, diffY - diffY // 2])
        x = torch.cat([x2, x1], dim=1)
        return self.conv(x)

class OutConv(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels):
        super(OutConv, self).__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.conv(x)

class unet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_classes, n_channels=14, bilinear=True):
        super(unet, self).__init__()
        self.n_channels = n_channels
        self.n_classes = n_classes
        self.bilinear = bilinear

        self.inc = DoubleConv(n_channels, 64)
        self.down1 = Down(64, 128)
        self.down2 = Down(128, 256)
        self.down3 = Down(256, 512)
        factor = 2 if bilinear else 1
        self.down4 = Down(512, 1024 // factor)
        self.up1 = Up(1024, 512 // factor, bilinear)
        self.up2 = Up(512, 256 // factor, bilinear)
        self.up3 = Up(256, 128 // factor, bilinear)
        self.up4 = Up(128, 64, bilinear)
        self.outc = OutConv(64, n_classes)

    def forward(self, x):
        x1 = self.inc(x)
        x2 = self.down1(x1)
        x3 = self.down2(x2)
        x4 = self.down3(x3)
        x5 = self.down4(x4)
        x = self.up1(x5, x4)
        x = self.up2(x, x3)
        x = self.up3(x, x2)
        x = self.up4(x, x1)
        logits = self.outc(x)
        return logits
    
def eval_image(predict,label,num_classes):
    index = np.where((label>=0) & (label<num_classes))
    predict = predict[index]
    label = label[index] 
    
    TP = np.zeros((num_classes, 1))
    FP = np.zeros((num_classes, 1))
    TN = np.zeros((num_classes, 1))
    FN = np.zeros((num_classes, 1))
    
    for i in range(0,num_classes):
        TP[i] = np.sum(label[np.where(predict==i)]==i)
        FP[i] = np.sum(label[np.where(predict==i)]!=i)
        TN[i] = np.sum(label[np.where(predict!=i)]!=i)
        FN[i] = np.sum(label[np.where(predict!=i)]==i)        
    
    return TP,FP,TN,FN,len(label)

# Model Initialization

# CNN-based models:
# 1."unet"
# 2."fcn", "fcn_rgb"
# 3."deeplabv3", "deeplabv3_rgb"
# 4."unet_geo"

# Transformer-based models:

# 6."swin", "swin_rgb"

model_name = "unet"   

num_classes = 2

if model_name == "unet":
    model = unet(n_classes=num_classes)

elif model_name in ["fcn", "fcn_rgb"]:
    weights = "COCO_WITH_VOC_LABELS_V1" if model_name == "fcn_rgb" else None
    model = seg_models.fcn_resnet50(weights=weights)
    if model_name == "fcn":
        model.band_reduction = nn.Conv2d(14, 3, kernel_size=1)
    model.classifier[4] = nn.Conv2d(512, num_classes, kernel_size=1)

elif model_name in ["deeplabv3", "deeplabv3_rgb"]:
    weights = "COCO_WITH_VOC_LABELS_V1" if model_name == "deeplabv3_rgb" else None
    model = seg_models.deeplabv3_resnet50(weights=weights)
    if model_name == "deeplabv3":
        model.band_reduction = nn.Conv2d(14, 3, kernel_size=1)
    model.classifier[4] = nn.Conv2d(256, num_classes, kernel_size=1)

elif model_name == "unet_geo":
    model = unet_geo(in_channels=14, classes=num_classes)
    
elif model_name in ["segformer", "segformer_rgb"]:
    model = SegformerForSemanticSegmentation.from_pretrained(
        "nvidia/segformer-b0-finetuned-ade-512-512",
        num_labels=num_classes,
        ignore_mismatched_sizes=True
    )
    if model_name == "segformer":
        model.band_reduction = nn.Conv2d(14, 3, kernel_size=1)

elif model_name in ["swin", "swin_rgb"]:
    model = UperNetForSemanticSegmentation.from_pretrained(
        "openmmlab/upernet-swin-tiny",
        num_labels=num_classes,
        ignore_mismatched_sizes=True
    )
    if model_name == "swin":
        model.band_reduction = nn.Conv2d(14, 3, kernel_size=1)

model = model.to(device)

optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate, weight_decay=5e-4)
weights = torch.tensor([1.0, 3.0]).to(device)
cross_entropy_loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(weight=weights, ignore_index=255)
In [10]:
interp = nn.Upsample(size=(input_size[1], input_size[0]), mode="bilinear")
hist = np.zeros((num_steps_stop, 3))
F1_best = 0.0

# handle different output formats across architectures
def forward_pass(model, images, model_name, interp):

    if model_name in ["fcn_rgb", "deeplabv3_rgb", "segformer_rgb", "swin_rgb"]:
        # B4 (R), B3 (G), B2 (B)
        images = images[:, [3, 2, 1], :, :]
    
    if model_name in ["fcn", "deeplabv3", "segformer", "swin"]:
        images = model.band_reduction(images)
    
    if model_name in ["segformer", "segformer_rgb", "swin", "swin_rgb"]:
        pred = model(images).logits
    else:
        pred = model(images)

    if isinstance(pred, dict):  # FCN / DeepLab
        pred = pred["out"]

    pred = interp(pred)
    return pred

def train_step(model, images, labels, optimizer, criterion, model_name, interp):
    model.train()
    optimizer.zero_grad()

    pred = forward_pass(model, images, model_name, interp)
    loss = criterion(pred, labels)

    _, pred_label = torch.max(pred, 1)
    pred_np = pred_label.detach().cpu().numpy()
    labels_np = labels.cpu().numpy()

    batch_oa = np.sum(pred_np == labels_np) / labels_np.size

    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()

    return loss.item(), batch_oa

def evaluate_model(model, test_loader, model_name, interp, epsilon, name_classes, device):
    print("Testing..........")
    model.eval()

    TP_all = np.zeros((2, 1))
    FP_all = np.zeros((2, 1))
    TN_all = np.zeros((2, 1))
    FN_all = np.zeros((2, 1))
    n_valid_sample_all = 0
    F1 = np.zeros((2, 1))

    for _, batch in enumerate(test_loader):
        image, label, _, name = batch
        label = label.squeeze().numpy()
        image = image.float().to(device)

        with torch.no_grad():
            pred = forward_pass(model, image, model_name, interp)

        _, pred = torch.max(nn.functional.softmax(pred, dim=1).detach(), 1)
        pred = pred.squeeze().data.cpu().numpy()

        TP, FP, TN, FN, n_valid_sample = eval_image(pred.reshape(-1), label.reshape(-1), 2)
        TP_all += TP
        FP_all += FP
        TN_all += TN
        FN_all += FN
        n_valid_sample_all += n_valid_sample
        
    OA = np.sum(TP_all) * 1.0 / n_valid_sample_all
    for i in range(2):
        P = TP_all[i] * 1.0 / (TP_all[i] + FP_all[i] + epsilon)
        R = TP_all[i] * 1.0 / (TP_all[i] + FN_all[i] + epsilon)
        F1[i] = 2.0 * P * R / (P + R + epsilon)
        if i == 1:
            print("===>" + name_classes[i] + " Precision: %.2f" % (P.item() * 100))
            print("===>" + name_classes[i] + " Recall: %.2f" % (R.item() * 100))
            print("===>" + name_classes[i] + " F1: %.2f" % (F1[i].item() * 100))

    mF1 = np.mean(F1)
    print("===> mean F1: %.2f OA: %.2f" % (mF1 * 100, OA * 100))

    return F1, OA, mF1

# saving the best checkpoint
def update_best(model, F1, F1_best, model_name):
    if F1[1].item() > F1_best:
        F1_best = F1[1].item()
        
        # Optional: save best model checkpoint
        # Disabled by default to avoid unintended overwrites during repeated experiments
        
        # print("Save Model")
        # checkpoint_name = f"best_{model_name}_landslide_F1.pth"
        # torch.save(model.state_dict(), checkpoint_name)
    
    return F1_best

# training loop with periodic evaluation
for batch_id, src_data in enumerate(src_loader):
    if batch_id == num_steps_stop:
        break
    start_time = time.time()
    images, labels, _, _ = src_data
    images = images.to(device)
    labels = labels.to(device).long()

    loss_value, batch_oa = train_step(model, images, labels, optimizer, cross_entropy_loss, model_name, interp)

    hist[batch_id, 0] = loss_value
    hist[batch_id, 1] = batch_oa
    hist[batch_id, 2] = time.time() - start_time

    if (batch_id + 1) % 10 == 0:
        print(
            "Iter %d/%d Time cost per iter: %.2f Batch_OA = %.1f cross_entropy_loss = %.3f"
            % (
                batch_id + 1,
                num_steps_stop,
                10 * np.mean(hist[batch_id - 9:batch_id + 1, 2]),
                np.mean(hist[batch_id - 9:batch_id + 1, 1]) * 100,
                np.mean(hist[batch_id - 9:batch_id + 1, 0])
            )
        )

    if (batch_id + 1) % 100 == 0:
        F1, OA, mF1 = evaluate_model(model, test_loader, model_name, interp, epsilon, name_classes, device)
        F1_best = update_best(model, F1, F1_best, model_name)

Experimental Notes¶

Several variations were explored to identify factors that meaningfully impact landslide segmentation performance beyond the baseline.

  • Training dynamics showed clear early convergence (100 - 300 epochs); extending to 300 epochs yielded no improvement and slight degradation, indicating limited benefit from prolonged optimization.
  • Optimization settings were fixed across experiments to ensure a fair comparison, focusing the analysis on architectural, spectral, and loss-design effects rather than hyperparameter tuning; no evidence suggests that optimization is the primary bottleneck, although some variability across runs indicates sensitivity to training dynamics.
  • Class-weighted CrossEntropy improved landslide detection under strong imbalance; moderate weighting (w = 3) balanced precision–recall, while low weighting led to under-detection (↑FN, ↓recall), and excessive weighting (w ≥ 10) caused overprediction (↑FP, ↓precision), reducing overall F1.
  • Very long training provided only marginal gains, suggesting performance is not iteration-limited but driven by proper loss design. For fair comparison, all models were evaluated at 300 epochs, as more complex architectures typically require longer training to stabilize.
  • Data augmentation (flip, rotation, scale/crop) consistently degraded performance, with rotations and flips causing the largest drops, indicating lack of rotation invariance and sensitivity to spatial transformations.
  • The negative effect of geometric augmentation suggests direction-dependent physical information in the data, making spatial transformations harmful.
  • Model comparison revealed a clear hierarchy (U-Net > SegFormer > Swin > DeepLabV3 ≈ FCN), indicating better generalization of simpler architectures under limited data.
  • Learned spectral projection (14 → 3) improved CNN performance over direct multispectral input, demonstrating that compact spectral compression can be beneficial.
  • RGB-pretrained weights degraded performance under projected multispectral input, suggesting a mismatch between pretrained filters and transformed spectral distributions.
  • In contrast, pretrained weights improved performance under RGB-only input, confirming that transfer learning is effective when the input distribution aligns with RGB-based pretraining (e.g., ImageNet).

n = len(saved_samples)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(n, 8, figsize=(15, 2.0 * n))

if n == 1:
    axes = axes[np.newaxis, :]

for i, (img, gt, pred) in enumerate(saved_samples):

    # --- Optical RGB composite (Sentinel-2: B4, B3, B2) ---
    rgb = np.stack([img[3], img[2], img[1]], axis=-1)
    rgb = (rgb - np.percentile(rgb, 2)) / (np.percentile(rgb, 98) - np.percentile(rgb, 2) + 1e-6)
    rgb = np.clip(rgb, 0, 1)
    
    axes[i, 0].imshow(rgb)
    axes[i, 0].set_title("Optical (RGB)")
    axes[i, 0].axis("off")

    # --- Band 8 (NIR) ---
    axes[i, 1].imshow(img[7], cmap="gray")
    axes[i, 1].set_title("Band 8 (NIR)")
    axes[i, 1].axis("off")

    # --- Band 11 (SWIR) ---
    axes[i, 2].imshow(img[10], cmap="gray")
    axes[i, 2].set_title("Band 11 (SWIR)")
    axes[i, 2].axis("off")

    # --- Slope ---
    axes[i, 3].imshow(img[12], cmap="terrain")
    axes[i, 3].set_title("Slope")
    axes[i, 3].axis("off")

    # --- DEM ---
    axes[i, 4].imshow(img[13], cmap="terrain")
    axes[i, 4].set_title("DEM")
    axes[i, 4].axis("off")

    # --- Landslide mask (Ground Truth) ---
    gt_rgb = index2bgr_z(gt).copy()
    gt_rgb[[0, -1], :, :] = 0
    gt_rgb[:, [0, -1], :] = 0

    axes[i, 5].imshow(gt_rgb)
    axes[i, 5].set_title("Landslide Mask")
    axes[i, 5].axis("off")

    # --- Prediction ---
    pred_rgb = index2bgr_z(pred).copy()
    pred_rgb[[0, -1], :, :] = 0
    pred_rgb[:, [0, -1], :] = 0

    axes[i, 6].imshow(pred_rgb)
    axes[i, 6].set_title("Prediction")
    axes[i, 6].axis("off")

    # --- Error Overlay (TP / FP / FN) ---
    tp = (pred == 1) & (gt == 1)
    fp = (pred == 1) & (gt == 0)
    fn = (pred == 0) & (gt == 1)

    overlay = np.zeros((*pred.shape, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    overlay[tp] = [0, 255, 0]   # Green = True Positive
    overlay[fp] = [255, 0, 0]   # Red   = False Positive
    overlay[fn] = [0, 0, 255]   # Blue  = False Negative

    axes[i, 7].imshow(overlay)
    axes[i, 7].set_title("TP (G) / FP (R) / FN (B)")
    axes[i, 7].axis("off")

fig.tight_layout(h_pad=1.5)
plt.show()

Peak Performance (100 Epochs – Early Convergence)¶

Model Input Strategy Landslide F1 (%) Mean F1 (%) OA (%) Note
U-Net 14 bands (direct) 63.01 81.09 98.39 Best observed performance

Key observations:

  • Landslide F1 is the primary evaluation metric due to strong class imbalance; OA and Mean F1 may obscure minority-class performance differences
  • U-Net provides the most consistent high performance under small-data conditions, with the best peak result observed
  • Learned spectral projection (14→3) improves CNN performance over direct multispectral input
  • Transformer-based models (SegFormer, Swin) remain competitive but do not show clear advantage in this small-data regime
  • RGB-only input consistently underperforms, confirming the importance of multispectral information
  • Performance differences are driven more by input representation than architectural complexity

Conclusion¶

  • Simple CNN-based architectures show more consistent performance than more complex models under limited data
  • Results show moderate variance across runs, consistent with small-data training dynamics.
  • Data characteristics (class imbalance and direction-dependent spatial structure) dominate performance; careful loss design is required, while geometric augmentation can degrade results
  • Proper handling of multispectral input is critical for performance
  • Increasing model complexity does not guarantee improvement without sufficient data scale
  • Performance is driven more by input representation and controlled evaluation than architectural novelty

This study highlights that, under small-data multispectral EO conditions, model performance is primarily determined by input representation and training setup, with simpler CNN-based approaches providing the most reliable results.
